title: On-call handoff notes - Lexi Martin
content:
Context:
- Shift: Feb 15 2026 handoff notes. Took the 18:00-02:00 UTC slot. Leaving notes for next oncall.
- Current major items: intermittent latency spikes observed on hosted-api model inference (gen-* routes) starting 2026-02-14 21:30 UTC. PagerDuty INC PD-4821 created.

Summary of status:
- Severity: Sev2 (partial degradation for some customers; majority traffic ok).
- Affected: hosted-api gen and chat routes for models served from us-west-2 cluster gw-usw2-01.
- Impact window: spikes every ~7-12 minutes lasting 20-45 seconds, CPU on GPU gateway nodes jumps and queue length increases.
- Temporary mitigation: scaling gateway pool to +2 instances reduces error rate; KV cache warmup seems to help.

What I did during shift (timeline):
- 21:37 UTC: Noticed elevated 5xx% on dashboards. Opened PD-4821 and posted to #sre-oncall.
- 21:40 UTC: Checked gw-usw2-01 pods: kubectl get pods -n inference-gateway -l app=gateway -o wide -> saw 2 pods OOMKilled in last 24h.
- 21:55 UTC: Scaled gateway-deployment from 8 -> 10 replicas (kubectl scale deploy gateway-deployment --replicas=10 -n inference-gateway).
- 22:05 UTC: Errors decreased; latency still spiky. Started cpu/memory profiling (pprof) on one gateway instance.
- 22:30 UTC: Correlated with nightly batch job INF-125 that kicks off heavy model warmup; added annotation to batch job to spread across nodes (temporary fix).
- 23:10 UTC: Restarted one problematic gateway pod to pick up new image (image tag: gateway:2026-02-12-hotfix).
- 00:45 UTC: Observed KV cache miss rate dropped after warmup changes; issue largely stabilized but not closed.

Open action items (for next oncall):
- Monitor PD-4821 until stable for 48h with no recurrence.
- If spikes return, immediately scale gateway-deployment to 14 replicas while investigating heap/GC.
- Run heap dump on any gateway pod that shows > 70% memory for 3 consecutive minutes: kubectl exec -it <pod> -n inference-gateway -- /bin/sh -c 'curl -sS http://localhost:6060/debug/pprof/heap > /tmp/heap-$(date +%s).pprof' (upload to S3 bucket s3://redwood-dumps/oncall).
- Check nightly batch job INF-125 schedule (confluence link above) and consider shifting to a different time window if correlated.

Temporary procedures (draft runbook snippets to be formalized):
1) Initial triage checklist:
   - Check PD incident details and run basic health checks:
     * kubectl get pods -n inference-gateway -o wide
     * kubectl top pods -n inference-gateway
     * curl -sS https://internal-metrics.redwood/api/p90?service=gateway
   - Post a short update to #sre-oncall with observed symptoms and steps taken.
2) Fast mitigation (if user-facing errors >1%):
   - Scale gateway: kubectl scale deploy gateway-deployment --replicas=<current+4> -n inference-gateway
   - If scaling does not reduce errors within 5 minutes, toggle routing to fallback region: runbooks/route-fallback (placeholder) - reach out to eng-routing on Slack.
3) Capturing diagnostics:
   - Increase log level on one gateway pod for 5 minutes: kubectl set env deploy/gateway-deployment LOG_LEVEL=debug -n inference-gateway (remember to revert).
   - Grab pprof CPU for 60s: curl -sS http://<pod-ip>:6060/debug/pprof/profile?seconds=60 > /tmp/cpu.pprof

Escalation contacts (in order):
- SRE lead: Aisha Patel (pager: +1-415-555-0132, slack: @aisha)
- Serving runtime oncall: Mason Lee (slack: @mason)
- Platform infra: Rahul Gupta (email: rahul@redwood.ai)

Notes-to-self / loose thoughts:
- The pattern looks like periodic batch warmups causing transient resource pressure; long-term fix might be to throttle warmups or pre-warm on dedicated nodes.
- Explore adding a rate limiter on the gateway queue to smooth bursts (ticket idea: INF-203).
- Verify that autoscaler policies have proper headroom during peak warmups (current minReplicas=6 looks low).

Commands & quick snippets (copy/paste):
- Check pods: kubectl get pods -n inference-gateway -o wide --sort-by=.status.containerStatuses[0].restartCount
- Scale: kubectl scale deploy gateway-deployment --replicas=10 -n inference-gateway
- Heap dump: kubectl exec -it <pod> -n inference-gateway -- /bin/sh -c 'curl -sS http://localhost:6060/debug/pprof/heap > /tmp/heap-$(date +%s).pprof'
- Upload to S3: aws s3 cp /tmp/heap-*.pprof s3://redwood-dumps/oncall/ --profile redwood-oncall

Drafts for runbook (to finish later):
- Formalize "gateway spike" runbook with thresholds, exact commands, and rollback steps.
- Add a decision tree for when to enable cross-region fallback.

Conversation pointers / links: 
- Slack thread: #sre-oncall thread ts: 1707957623 (see slack link in linked_artifacts)
- Confluence page with INF-125 details: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/SRE/kv-cache-issues

Final handoff checklist (what I'm leaving for next person):
- PD-4821 updated with actions; set to "monitoring" state.
- Gateway deployment scaled to 10 replicas.
- Batch INF-125 annotated to spread jobs.
- Heap dumps uploaded for two pods: s3://redwood-dumps/oncall/heap-1613.pprof, heap-1627.pprof
- Ping Aisha if anything reoccurs.

If you pick this up: start from the top, give a short update in #sre-oncall with current metrics and that you're taking over. If anything is unclear ping me (slack: @lexi) - I'll be slower tonight but will respond within 30-60m.

-- Lexi
